newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac says govt stance similar to own.
newsitem.headline: Westpac says govt stance similar to own.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corporation said on Wednesday the government's response to the Wallis inquiry's recommendation on bank mergers was broadly in line with its own position.
"The government's response appears to be broadly in line with Westpac's position on efficiency benefits of mergers," Westpac's managing director Bob Joss said in a statement.

"However, the government has decided to move cautiously on the timing of any relaxation of mergers between the major banks, pending demonstrated increased competition from the implementation of the inquiry's recommendations," Joss said.
The Wallis inquiry recommended that the "six pillars" policy, which prevented mergers among the four biggest banks and two largest life companies, should be removed.
Treasurer Peter Costello said the government had decided to end the "six pillars" policy, but ruled out mergers between the big four banks at present.
This would be reviewed when the government was satisfied that competition, particularly in small business lending, had increased sufficiently to allow such mergers to be considered, he said.
Joss said responses to the detailed recommendations of the Wallis inquiry needed careful consideration.
Westpac last week launched a A$1.435 billion friendly bid for the Bank of Melbourne, which operates in the state of Victoria.
Analysts said the Wallis inquiry should have little impact on the bid, with a final ruling to be determined by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
Westpac shares closed 20 cents lower at A$6.67.
